To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ciliotoxicity was observed for a large group of compounds that were structurally diverse.
316 individual compounds of tobacco smoke, tested in vitro at 5 mM, cause ciliostatic effects on the chicken tracheal cilia.

the majority of compounds tested in the study were found to cause reversible ciliostasis in chicken tracheal cultures at 5 mM, and that the ciliostatic activity was found to correlate well with the chemical structure and physical properties of the compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the compounds in tobacco smoke that cause the respiratory irritation and damage.
the identification of ciliotoxic compounds in the smoke of cigarettes.
the effects of individual compounds representative of tobacco smoke on the ciliary function of the embryonic chicken trachea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compounds which are ciliotoxic in vitro, are also present in tobacco smoke and may be important in the development of chronic obstructive lung disease.
the ciliotoxicity profile of tobacco smoke is dominated by the presence of a large number of compounds with a high degree of structural similarity, i.e. the phenylethers.

the ciliotoxicity is a property of many of the tobacco smoke components and is related to a variety of structural types, including alcohols, phenolic ethers, aldehydes and ketones, and nitriles, but not of benzoic acid derivatives and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compounds with a molecular mass of less than 200, with the exception of the benzonitriles and the alpha, beta- unsaturated aldehydes and ketones, were not ciliotoxic.
the compounds with a high degree of ciliotoxicity are either aromatic in nature and/or possess a carbonyl function.
the majority of the compounds that were tested in the present study were found to be ciliotoxic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ciliary activity of chicken tracheal epithelium can be inhibited in vitro by a wide range of compounds, including those that are present in tobacco smoke at concentrations that are relevant to human exposure.
the compounds causing ciliostasis were not necessarily the most abundant compounds in tobacco smoke, but were rather the most potent compounds in the smoke.
the majority of the compounds that were tested are not ciliotoxic at concentrations that are relevant for the human exposure.
